newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Sanevit posts higher 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Romania Sanevit posts higher 1996 profit.

text.p: Romanian listed syringe maker Sanevit reported a 1.187 billion lei net profit for 1996, up from 518 million last year.
A company report sent to the Bucharest bourse said Sanevit would pay its shareholders a 444 lei per share dividend. Last year, the company paid zero dividends.
The report ended a four-session bourse suspension on Tuesday pending the release of details on the latest meeting of Sanevit stockholders.
Sanevit, Romania's sole maker of disposable syringes, started production in April 1995, but has yet to achieve targeted annual output of 180 million syringes and 400 million needles.
Its 1996 output was 57 million syringes and more than 153 million needles, the report showed, and planned output for 1997 was 125 million syringes and 390 million needles.
The domestic market can absorb up to 300 million syringes and 400 million needles a year.

Sanevit, based in the Transylvanian city of Arad, entered the capital market when the bourse opened in November 1995 as its sole private stock. It dominated trading for a few months, but fell sharply throughout 1996.
On Wednesday, it closed at 8,600 lei, 400 weaker on its quote before suspension. When it joined the bourse it had a price of 71,000 lei. ($=7,025 lei)
